summary: Sudden multi-region 5xx plateau during short-lived streaming session flood; upstream proxy FD exhaustion
description:
Issue summary:

Customer Kepler Health reported a sudden and sustained rise in 5xx responses impacting chat streaming endpoints during an evening traffic spike. The burst consisted primarily of many short-lived streaming sessions (3–15s each) from client-side reconnect behavior. Impact: customer reports ~40% of streaming requests returning 502/503, degraded throughput, and increased tail latency.

Impact:
- Multiple customers in us-east observing elevated 5xx and failed streaming sessions.
- Kepler Health reports production outages for their chat feature across ~45% of sessions during the spike window.
- Billing unaffected, but SLA risk and customer-facing errors.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster serving mix of chat and small-embedding workloads
- Model in use: rw/open-instruct-3b pinned v2026-02-28
- API Gateway version: apigw-2.3.14
- Runtime proxy: realtime-proxy v1.8.2
- Serving runtime: inferd-0.9.7

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate 2k concurrent short-lived streaming sessions across pooled clients, reconnecting with backoff disabled.
2) Observe accept-queue growth on apigw, increases in half-closed sockets and short-lived TLS handshakes.
3) Watch realtime-proxy FD usage climb until accept() / epoll returns EMFILE and upstreams return 502/503.

Observed behavior and logs: 
- apigw metrics: accept queue length spiked from ~20 to 800 within 45s; connection resets increased sharply.
- realtime-proxy host logs: repeated "Too many open files" and "accept failed: EMFILE" messages on multiple pods.
- kernel: per-process FD count peaked ~120k on several proxy pods (limit configured at 64k); OS killed some proxy worker threads leading to 502s.
- serving-runtime telemetry: GPU scheduling latency rose as many requests entered the queue; watchdog triggered several soft restarts when runtimes blocked on socket I/O.
- No immediate OOM on GPUs, but higher GPU utilization and longer queueing times.

Initial customer-provided timestamps: 2026-03-10T20:12:00Z to 2026-03-10T20:28:00Z.

2026-03-10 20:40 - Eng (Lina): Temporary mitigation: increased proxy max_fds to 200k on affected nodes and bumped system-wide ulimit. Applied at 20:35; partial reduction in 502s but root cause still present.

investigation_notes: Connection churn pattern: majority of sessions were < 20s and clients retried aggressively (0s initial backoff) which amplified handshake rate.
Proxy behavior: V1.8.2 does not reliably close peer FDs when client initiates TLS renegotiation and then immediately closes; leak accumulates under high churn.
Kernel limits: node-level file descriptor soft limit set to 64k which was exceeded by the prolonged leak; increasing ulimit helped but is not a long-term fix.
API Gateway: accept queue growth exposed proxy to a flood of half-open sockets instead of steady connections, making leak visible much faster.
Serving runtime: worker threads blocked on socket ops increased watchdog restarts when backlog grew and prefetchers contended for NVMe I/O.
Repro: Local stress test reproduced EMFILE within 30–60s using the client's reconnect pattern; patched proxy in staging prevented the leak.
Telemetry: per-pod FD count, accept queue length, tls-handshake-rate, and EMFILE/error counts are effective indicators for future alerting.
workaround: Short-term mitigations applied: 1) Increased proxy ulimit to 200k on affected nodes; 2) Autoscaled proxy pool and added fast-surge capacity; 3) Deployed per-tenant connection-rate limits at apigw to smooth handshake bursts; 4) Advised customer to add exponential reconnect backoff. These mitigations stabilized customer impact within ~10 minutes.
root_cause: A file-descriptor leak in realtime-proxy v1.8.2 that manifests during high TLS handshake churn and half-closed client connections. The leak causes per-process FD exhaustion (EMFILE) which prevents accept() from succeeding, leading to 502/503 responses from API Gateway and additional runtime queueing that triggered watchdog restarts.
resolution: Patch merged to close leaked descriptors during TLS renegotiation edge-cases (PR referenced above). Canary rolled to 10% on 2026-03-12 09:30 and expanded to 100% by 2026-03-12 16:00 after confirmation of stability. Added alerting for rapid FD growth and an apigw circuit that enforces handshake-rate limits. Post-deploy telemetry shows no further EMFILE spikes and error rates returned to baseline.
next_steps: Finalize postmortem and publish to Confluence including timeline and customer impact summary.
Add automated stress test simulating short-lived streaming reconnection patterns to CI for realtime-proxy.
Permanent change: harden proxy to gracefully drop half-open sockets earlier and add unit tests for FD cleanup paths.
Operational: add FD-growth alert and a circuit-breaker in apigw to temporarily throttle handshake rate per-tenant.
CS follow-up: coordinate SLA credit review with Finance and Customer Success for Kepler Health.
